title.narrative: Resilient Environment Program: Climate Adaptation of Fluminense Cities

description.narrative:
This project aims to expand the engagement of Rio de Janeiro State’s Direct and Indirect Administration in establishing a culture of sustainability that increases urban resilience through the development of disaster-risk reduction and mitigation actions.
This proposal complements the “Inclusive and Sustainable Rio” project, which is currently underway and focuses on strengthening the 2030 Agenda and NUA principles and the inclusion and sustainability of the State of Rio de Janeiro through activities to strengthen technical capacities, improvement and standardization of monitoring systems and use of data, innovation in public management and community mobilization and participation.
To achieve the proposed goal, the State Government of Rio de Janeiro (GERJ) proposes a partnership with the United Nations Programme for Human Settlements (UN-Habitat) focused on the following:
Objective: By 2030, Rio de Janeiro's municipalities and local communities have significantly reduced climate and environmental hazard-related loss and damage across the state.
Outcome 1: Enhance the capacity of municipalities and local communities in Rio de Janeiro to prevent, prepare for, respond to, and adapt to climate and environmental challenges, while mitigating disasters across the state.
Output 1.1: Technical training program held with the 92 municipalities in Rio de Janeiro to identify, assess and manage climate risks Output 1.2: Study of flood risks in the state of Rio de Janeiro conducted Output 1.3: Municipal Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience Plans for 25 priority municipalities elaborated Output 1.4: School resilience and risk mitigation program carried out Output 1.5: Nine (9) climate-related project concept notes for financing opportunities elaborated Output 1.6: Ten (10) Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) pilots developed Output 1.7: One (1) pilot project using the "Sponge City" concept developed
The project will operate across the nine hydrographic regions of the state, ensuring a comprehensive approach to water resource management. The National Water Resources Policy (Law 9.433/1997) established the watershed as the planning unit for implementing water resource management, and other environmental legislation followed the same principle. This decision enabled a systematic planning approach for the multiple uses of water, joint actions for environmental conservation and restoration, and encouraged the participation of local communities in decision-making, aiming to reconcile sustainable development with the conservation of natural resources.
